rows.title: Colorado oil and gas regulators reject two drilling plans deemed too close to people and pronghorns
rows.standfirst: One plan was for a remote and pristine part of Weld County prairie, another for a developed area of homes and parks between Broomfield and Erie

rows.title: Colorado short-term rental owners opposed to effort to quadruple their taxes plan to descend upon Capitol in protest
rows.standfirst: A survey of 2,500 short-term rental owners, commissioned by an advocacy group, showed that a majority would reduce their rental nights if Senate Bill 33 passes. The measure is likely to be heavily amended, however.

rows.title: What’s Working | How the pandemic helped provide permanent funding for rural Colorado’s economic development
rows.standfirst: What’s ROO and how it became part of state law. Plus: The number of job openings in Colorado may be in decline but there’s still a lot. The types of openings, though, are changing.

rows.title: More than $150M has been invested in Trinidad. Has it worked?
rows.standfirst: Tension between the old guard and the new has stalled progress as the town looks for an economic renaissance

rows.title: Colorado hospitals’ profits plunged roughly 90% in 2022
rows.standfirst: The state says most hospitals have strong cash reserves, but hospitals say the financial picture hasn’t improved much

rows.title: Colorado lawmakers seek to boost condo development by reducing lawsuits over construction errors
rows.standfirst: Condos are seen as a key way to ease Colorado’s housing affordability crisis, but changing the state’s so-called construction defects laws has been a political third rail

rows.title: Discounted internet on track to end for 250,000 Colorado households in April
rows.standfirst: The Affordable Connectivity Program will stop accepting newcomers Feb. 7. Advocates hope Congress will extend funding.

rows.title: Colorado’s unused $8M in rental assistance funding could have been spent in a week, officials say
rows.standfirst: The fight over rental assistance spilled onto the Senate floor Tuesday, with lawmakers from both parties blasting the Polis administration for its refusal to spend $8 million in rental assistance money

rows.title: Colorado AG settles with Marriott over hidden hotel fees
rows.standfirst: Resort fees aren’t illegal, but hiding them as consumers plan their overnight stays violates the state’s Consumer Protection Act. The FTC is also working to address “junk” fees.

rows.title: Tri-State and United Power closer than ever to breakup agreement after 4 years of fighting
rows.standfirst: Tri-State and its largest member disagree over the cost to get out of a 50-year contract to purchase electricity

rows.title: Denver cuts services in response to the migrant crisis that’s costing the city $180 million
rows.standfirst: Denver Mayor Mike Johnston announced cuts to the DMV and Parks & Recreation in response to the migrant crisis.

rows.title: What’s Working: Colorado ranked as one of the top states for protecting consumer data, but it still gets a C+
rows.standfirst: That’s a tough grading curve, Colorado AG says of consumer-advocacy group’s report card. Plus: Protecting consumer neural data, other proposed privacy bills and more!

rows.title: An unusually comprehensive collection of northern Colorado artifacts sits dormant. Will it ever reopen?
rows.standfirst: The Bee Family Centennial Farm Museum — one family’s rare slice of the state’s agricultural history — faces an existential crisis

rows.title: She started fishing to connect with her late husband. She started a company because of the problems she ran into.
rows.standfirst: Fort Collins woman starts fly-fishing company to introduce other women to the sport and the peace it brings her

rows.title: A little worm destroyed last year’s sweet corn crop. Here’s how Colorado farmers are fighting back.
rows.standfirst: Tuxedo Corn and other growers around Olathe have been working on a trio of responses to try to thwart — or at least slow down — the corn earworm

rows.title: More than 600K pounds of electronic waste has been diverted from landfills thanks to Colorado teenagers
rows.standfirst: Over the past 12 years, Cañon City High School students have prepped and delivered mostly electronic waste to 3R Technology Solutions

rows.title: Colorado AG sues to block merger between parent companies of King Soopers and Safeway
rows.standfirst: After hosting town halls across the state, AG Phil Weiser said the merger would result in “higher prices, worse customer service”

rows.title: Denver has helped 40,000 migrants while Colorado Springs counts 24 families. Does being a sanctuary city matter that much?
rows.standfirst: El Paso County officials are loudly proclaiming that migrants are not welcome in Colorado’s 2nd-largest city, but the pronouncement has no legal bearing

rows.title: Two investors purchase Colorado Springs Independent to revive the defunct alt weekly newspaper
rows.standfirst: Longtime Colorado Springs businessmen announced their purchase about a month after the paper went dark amid overwhelming debt

rows.title: New $30M Colorado rental assistance program launches this week to stem unprecedented number of evictions
rows.standfirst: The first round of applications for the Temporary Rental Assistance Grant will be accepted until Feb. 20.

rows.title: What’s Working | Colorado’s current economy and a peek into the future
rows.standfirst: The ColoradoCast predicts what is likely to happen in the next six months. Plus: The latest on inflation, housing market, jobs and more!

rows.title: Beef, quality-stamped by an in-person grader, may soon be graded by someone looking at a picture
rows.standfirst: The USDA says its Remote Grading Pilot for Beef could give small packers and processors a leg up they desperately need.

rows.title: Rules to ensure there’s cash to plug all Colorado oil wells may not be enough, study says
rows.standfirst: Projected to raise $641 million to cap old wells and remediate sites, the new rules have loopholes that may make the final sum much smaller

rows.title: State funding could be withheld from Colorado cities that don’t tie housing to transit under new affordability push
rows.standfirst: The measure, House Bill 1313, is a key piece of Democratic Gov. Jared Polis’ plans to address the state’s housing shortage and combat climate change.

rows.title: Colorado Springs cracks down on homeless camping in hopes of pushing people toward shelter, services
rows.standfirst: While Denver police wrote 14 citations for illegal camping last year, Colorado Springs handed out 899 tickets

rows.title: Modular homebuilders are rallying to create affordable Colorado housing. Financial barriers are shutting some out.
rows.standfirst: Nick Lemmer and Ethan Deffenbaugh turned to state loans for the $8 million they needed to get their automated modular housing startup, Higher Purpose Homes, up and running. But urgency for units and high competition left the community-minded innovators lacking.

rows.title: A new — and much gentler — property tax hike is proposed for Colorado short-term rental properties
rows.standfirst: Rep. Shannon Bird says her House Bill 1299 “makes more sense” than Senate Bill 33, which would quadruple property taxes on short-term rental properties rented for more than 90 days a year. But it faces uncertain odds.

rows.title: Techstars moving HQ out of Colorado and ending its Boulder accelerator
rows.standfirst: It’s the end of an entrepreneurial era that helped turn the Boulder and Denver region into some of the nation’s top startup cities. But Techstars will still have a local presence.

rows.title: Postal Service floats idea of driving Western Slope mail to Denver and back before delivery
rows.standfirst: Angry customers, including county clerks, mayors and city managers, say proposal to modernize Grand Junction processing and save money spells trouble

rows.title: What’s Working: Techstars alumni, mentors consider what’s next for the Boulder/Denver startup community
rows.standfirst: The tech accelerator isn’t abandoning Colorado, just moving its HQ to New York. But what about the local community, asks the local community. Plus: Denver ranked … 71st for tech?

rows.title: Colorado has allocated millions of dollars this year to governments and housing organizations planning to build affordable units
rows.standfirst: Funds from Proposition 123, the 2022 ballot measure aiming to increase affordable housing stock in Colorado, are helping to create more of these units.

rows.title: Federal government sues to block merger of grocery giants Kroger and Albertsons, saying it could push prices higher
rows.standfirst: The Federal Trade Commission argued the deal would eliminate competition and hurt consumers

rows.title: Denver closing four shelters, scaling back migrant services to save $60M
rows.standfirst: As the hotel shelters close, the city says it will “double down” on case management by coordinating with nonprofits that are connecting migrants to jobs and housing

rows.title: Colorado’s largest private sector union violated federal labor law in treatment of its internal staff, judge rules
rows.standfirst: Former UFCW Local 7 employees interviewed by The Colorado Sun pointed the blame at union President Kim Cordova, who has been at the helm since 2010

rows.title: Adams County’s oil and gas rules are among Colorado’s strictest — and the industry is still rapidly growing
rows.standfirst: Since 2017, oil production has grown 15-fold as the county became Colorado’s second-biggest producer churning out 12.8 million barrels in 2023
